text:
Priya (Support): @Alex @Jonatan customer "AcmeApp" reporting huge tail latency since ~09:20 UTC for eu-west endpoints. Multiple p95/p99 spikes, API errors (504) intermittently. Raised from support: https://support/INC-9876 :rotating_light:

Alex (SRE): grabbing logs. Do we have region-level metrics? Any routing changes pushed around 09:15-09:25?

sre-bot: Automated alert: edge.p95.eu-west > 800ms for 15m, p99 > 1.6s. Ingress TLS handshakes spike detected.

Jonatan (Edge): I see an increase in TLS handshake time on our front proxies in eu-west-2, and some connections are landing in eu-central backends (cross-region). Could be anycast / DNS geo-steering behaving odd.

Maria (NetInfra): Confirmed BGP updates around 09:18 from upstream provider EU-IX; looks like one anycast POP announced with higher MED, causing some traffic to re-home -> extra cross-az hop. Pulling sflow sample.

Priya (Support): Customer provided curl timings and trace:```
$ curl -w "time_namelookup: %{time_namelookup}s
  time_connect: %{time_connect}s
  time_appconnect: %{time_appconnect}s
  time_pretransfer: %{time_pretransfer}s
  time_starttransfer: %{time_starttransfer}s
" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
time_namelookup: 0.072
time_connect: 0.153
time_appconnect: 1.12
time_pretransfer: 1.12
time_starttransfer: 1.63
HTTP/2 504
```

Alex (SRE): appconnect ~1.12s -> TLS handshake taking long. DNS lookup nonzero but small, so name resolution likely okay. That appconnect includes TCP + TLS. Need packet captures at edge proxy for sample client IP 34.81.10.55.

Jonatan (Edge): Running tcpdump on proxy-ew2-03 for that IP now. Also getting traceroute from customer:```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.29.14.7), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.4.0.1  0.4 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  198.51.100.7  5.6 ms  5.7 ms  5.8 ms
 3  203.0.113.45  12.9 ms  13.1 ms  12.8 ms
 4  52.29.14.7  120.3 ms  121.0 ms  120.6 ms
```

Maria (NetInfra): hop 4 120ms suggests traffic egressing to a different region or hairpin. Combined with BGP flaps earlier -> likely some clients are being steered to remote POPs.

Eric (Infra): I pulled edge proxy logs: timestamps around 09:18 show spike in SYN retries and TLS handshake timeouts:```
2026-03-14T09:18:22Z proxy-ew2-03 conn=12345 client=34.81.10.55 TLS handshake stage=ClientHello->ServerHello duration=1180ms
2026-03-14T09:18:22Z proxy-ew2-03 conn=12346 client=34.81.10.58 TLS handshake stage=ClientHello->ServerHello duration=1250ms
2026-03-14T09:18:23Z proxy-ew2-03 conn=12347 client=34.81.12.10 TLS handshake timeout
```

Jonatan (Edge): I see our TLS stack queuing up handshakes; CPU on proxy-ew2-03 is 90% due to a large burst of new connections (short TTLs causing reconnects). Could be upstream health-checking or a misconfigured load balancer causing re-connections.

Alex (SRE): Questions to triage: 1) Is this limited to eu-west? 2) Are anycast routes stable? 3) DNS TTL changed recently? 4) Any config deploy around 09:15?

Maria (NetInfra): Answers: 1) Most reports from eu-west but low-level noise in eu-central. 2) Anycast peering had a flapping session with Provider-A; route dampening hit briefly. 3) DNS TTL unchanged (60s). 4) No infra deploys at 09:15 in our deploy logs.

Priya (Support): Customer says degrade started at ~09:20 and affects 30% of their requests. They can repro by hitting eu-west endpoint. Asking for ETA and mitigations.

Jonatan (Edge): Immediate mitigations I can do: - rotate traffic off proxy-ew2-03 to other healthy proxies in eu-west - increase TLS worker threads on proxies temporarily - enable handshake backpressure to drop new inflight if CPU hits 95% - push a BGP path-preference to prefer POP-A over POP-B (but needs approval)

Alex (SRE): Actions we took: - rotated traffic away from proxy-ew2-03 at 09:31 (traffic-shift 30s ramp) - flushed local DNS cache on edge hosts to ensure correct anycast decisions - applied temporary TLS worker bump on proxies at 09:33

sre-bot: Action log: traffic-shift executed by Alex -> shifted ~22% traffic to proxy-ew2-01/02; TLS workers +25% on proxies in eu-west.

Priya (Support): Customer confirmed improved p95 after 09:36; still seeing occasional 500/504s but much better. :thumbsup:

Eric (Infra): Root cause analysis (prelim): upstream BGP instability caused transient anycast mis-ads that increased cross-region hops for a subset of clients, combined with a burst of short-lived connections which amplified TLS handshake CPU on one proxy. The combination produced p95/p99 latency regressions.

Alex (SRE): Follow-ups and next steps: - Ask Provider-A for BGP flap root cause and request more stable MED/communities. - Add longer BGP dampening threshold in our POPs to avoid quick rehome churn. - Increase default TLS worker pool headroom and add adaptive autoscaling for TLS handshakes. - Add metric: handshake-queue-length per proxy + alert when CPU>80% + queue>200. - Improve anycast monitoring: correlate route changes to p95 increases within 60s window.

Jonatan (Edge): Also adding a fast rollback playbook: if p99 > 1s AND anycast route churn detected -> automatic traffic-shift to regional non-anycast VIP for 60s while route stabilizes.

Maria (NetInfra): I'll open ticket with Provider-A and attach sFlow/samples. Also will schedule a config change window to tweak BGP damping after approval.

Priya (Support): I've updated customer with the mitigation and timeline. They'll reopen if they see resurgence. Logged actions in INC-9876.

Alex (SRE): Great. Closing loop: please drop any additional traces or client IPs here if you see more. Thanks team.

Customer: AcmeApp: Confirmed much better now from our side. We'll monitor for the next 24h and ping if it recurs. Thanks for the quick response! :pray:
